summary: Explains runas tries to use the become user's full (elevated) token and falls back to a limited token; SeDebugPrivilege (Administrators by default) is needed for elevation. Check the token with win_whoami.
questions: How do I check whether become on Windows got admin rights?
Why does become on Windows run with limited privileges?
What privilege is needed for an elevated become process on Windows?

answer_card.title: Administrative rights with runas
answer_card.answer_md:
`runas` tries to run with the become user's full privileges; if elevation fails it continues with a **limited token**. Elevation needs **`SeDebugPrivilege`** (Administrators have it by default).

Check what you got:

```yaml
- ansible.windows.win_whoami:
  become: true
```
